newsitem.title: USA: Allstate Q4 life statutory premiums up.
newsitem.headline: Allstate Q4 life statutory premiums up.

text.p: Allstate Corp said statutory premiums, which include all premiums and deposits, grew 6.3 percent in fourth quarter 1996.
This increase was driven by sales of new annuities, as well as universal life products, Allstate said.
Operating income increased 15.4 percent to $90 million due to growth in invested assets and favorable margins on existing business, according to Allstate.
Net income increased 45 percent to $87 million, compared with $60 million for the same period in 1995.

Revenues determined under generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) increased 7.3 percent as increases in traditional life insurance sales, sales of life contingent annuities, and lower realized capital losses contributed to the increase over the same period last year.
Statutory premiums increased 5.8 percent in 1996, reflecting higher sales of new annuities, as well as increased life product sales, Allstate said.

Revenues determined under GAAP increased 1.1 percent as increases in traditional life product sales, investment income, fee-based product revenues and realized capital gains were partially offset by lower sales of life contingent annuities.
Operating income increased 12.5 percent to $368 million due to growth in invested assets and favorable margins on existing business.
Net income increased 15.1 percent to $388 million, reflecting improved operating results and increased realized capital gains.
